canonical_definition:
Space of definitions. Across the papers, the dominant framing treats long-context understanding as a latent model ability to process, understand, retain, integrate, and use information across very long input sequences, often while maintaining coherence, relevance, accuracy, or task performance beyond the original context window. Many definitions make the span explicit, from long documents and multi-turn histories to contexts over 100K tokens, and some stress whole-context use, asking whether models can "fully utilize the provided information." A smaller line of work narrows the construct to particular settings or subskills, including cross-page synthesis, recall of specific facts from sparse long inputs, dialogue-history retention, or multimodal long text and video contexts.

Space of facets. Most papers use nearby labels such as long-context comprehension, long-text understanding, long-context capability, long-context modeling, and long-context processing for closely related versions of the same broad ability. More specialized labels carve out narrower facets: cross-page comprehension focuses on reasoning over evidence across pages, recall ability or long-range information access focuses on retrieving distant information, and context memory or long-context modeling capacity focuses on retaining and using dialogue history. Some papers also distinguish it from short-context ability, or place it alongside reasoning, retrieval, generation, and multimodal understanding in broader capability bundles.

Space of measurement. Operationalization is largely benchmark-based: papers link the construct to 48 measurement instruments and 17 behavioral indicators. The most common instruments are LongBench, RULER, InfiniteBench, Needle-in-a-Haystack, and L-Eval; in practice, papers measure it with multitask long-context benchmark suites, synthetic retrieval and variable-tracing tasks, ultra-long benchmarks over 100K tokens, document, question answering, summarization, multimodal, and video evaluations, and some long-form language-modeling datasets scored by perplexity. These operationalizations generally match the dominant definitions around processing and using long inputs, though some narrow the construct to recall- or retrieval-focused behavior rather than the broader notions of coherence or whole-context integration.

Links. The recorded links mix incoming and outgoing claims. Papers claim causal relationships from contextual understanding, long-range dependency modeling, and positional bias to long-context understanding, and from long-context understanding to text summarization; separate papers also report related links to length generalization. Correlational claims are rarer, including links to text summarization and memory, while other related claims connect it with neighboring long-context tasks and abilities.

characterization_sections.label: Space of definitions.
characterization_sections.text: Across the papers, the dominant framing treats long-context understanding as a latent model ability to process, understand, retain, integrate, and use information across very long input sequences, often while maintaining coherence, relevance, accuracy, or task performance beyond the original context window. Many definitions make the span explicit, from long documents and multi-turn histories to contexts over 100K tokens, and some stress whole-context use, asking whether models can "fully utilize the provided information." A smaller line of work narrows the construct to particular settings or subskills, including cross-page synthesis, recall of specific facts from sparse long inputs, dialogue-history retention, or multimodal long text and video contexts.

characterization_sections.label: Space of facets.
characterization_sections.text: Most papers use nearby labels such as long-context comprehension, long-text understanding, long-context capability, long-context modeling, and long-context processing for closely related versions of the same broad ability. More specialized labels carve out narrower facets: cross-page comprehension focuses on reasoning over evidence across pages, recall ability or long-range information access focuses on retrieving distant information, and context memory or long-context modeling capacity focuses on retaining and using dialogue history. Some papers also distinguish it from short-context ability, or place it alongside reasoning, retrieval, generation, and multimodal understanding in broader capability bundles.

characterization_sections.label: Space of measurement.
characterization_sections.text: Operationalization is largely benchmark-based: papers link the construct to 48 measurement instruments and 17 behavioral indicators. The most common instruments are LongBench, RULER, InfiniteBench, Needle-in-a-Haystack, and L-Eval; in practice, papers measure it with multitask long-context benchmark suites, synthetic retrieval and variable-tracing tasks, ultra-long benchmarks over 100K tokens, document, question answering, summarization, multimodal, and video evaluations, and some long-form language-modeling datasets scored by perplexity. These operationalizations generally match the dominant definitions around processing and using long inputs, though some narrow the construct to recall- or retrieval-focused behavior rather than the broader notions of coherence or whole-context integration.

characterization_sections.label: Links.
characterization_sections.text: The recorded links mix incoming and outgoing claims. Papers claim causal relationships from contextual understanding, long-range dependency modeling, and positional bias to long-context understanding, and from long-context understanding to text summarization; separate papers also report related links to length generalization. Correlational claims are rarer, including links to text summarization and memory, while other related claims connect it with neighboring long-context tasks and abilities.

definition_agreement.reason: Most papers define long-context understanding as a model's ability to process, retain, integrate, and use information distributed across very long input sequences, documents, or histories while maintaining coherence, accuracy, or task performance. A few papers emphasize particular settings or facets such as dialogue, multi-document evidence, multimodal inputs, retrieval-intensive recall, or contexts beyond the nominal window, but these are narrow applications or emphases of the same core property rather than different constructs.
